question: Qual é a ideia central de Safety by Design no documento de maio de 2019?
answer: Incorporar [[direitos e segurança dos usuários]] ao design e à funcionalidade de produtos e serviços desde o desenvolvimento. A segurança constitui um [[terceiro pilar]], ao lado de privacidade e segurança da informação, e um imperativo de design do produto.

source.title: Safety by Design Overview (May 2019)
evidence:
At its core, SbD is about embedding the rights

of users and user safety into the design and

functionality of products and services. It places

safety as the third pillar in the developmental

process, sitting alongside the well-established

processes of privacy and security. Safety is a

product design imperative.

question: Como o relatório descreve a consulta utilizada para desenvolver o framework?
answer: Uma consulta iniciada em junho de 2018 com [[indústria e organizações relacionadas, pais e cuidadores, e jovens de 14 a 17 anos]]. O objetivo era formular princípios significativos, práticos e alcançáveis, considerando pessoas que necessitam de proteção especial.

source.title: Safety by Design Overview (May 2019)
evidence:
In June 2018, eSafety undertook a three-pronged

consultation process to guide the development of

the SbD Framework. This included consultation with:

1. Industry and other companies, trade bodies

or representative organisations that were

identified as having synergies or an interest in

safeguarding users online.

2. Parents and carers.

3. Young people (aged 14-17).

The purpose of the consultation was to ensure

that the SbD Principles encapsulated all aspects

of user safety in a meaningful, achievable and

practical way. We felt it was imperative that the

Principles reflected the needs and expectations

of those in need of special protections, such as

children and young people and those in vulnerable

circumstances, as well as parents and carers.

question: Qual foi a participação de pais e jovens na consulta descrita?
answer: O relatório registra pesquisa com [[3.520 pais e responsáveis]] por crianças de 2 a 17 anos, em julho e agosto de 2018. Depois, houve um [[fórum online estruturado de cinco dias com 123 jovens]], de 14 a 17 anos.

source.title: Safety by Design Overview (May 2019)
evidence:
In July and August 2018, eSafety conducted a

nationally representative survey (2018 Parent

Survey) of 3,520 parents and guardians of children

aged 2 to 17 using multiple online panels (n=3,044)

and computer assisted telephone interviewing

(n=476).

Following the findings of the 2018 Parent Survey,

eSafety held a five-day, structured online

forum with 123 young people aged 14 to 17.

question: Quais são os três princípios gerais de Safety by Design no relatório?
answer: [[Responsabilidades do prestador do serviço]], [[empoderamento e autonomia do usuário]] e [[transparência e prestação de contas]]. Eles organizam orientações para considerar segurança no design, desenvolvimento e disponibilização dos serviços.

source.title: Safety by Design Overview (May 2019)
evidence:
The principles set out the measures that eSafety

encourages and envisages online and digital

services will take to ensure that the safety of

users is suitably addressed and considered during

the design, development and deployment of their

question: Que responsabilidade do prestador o primeiro princípio enfatiza?
answer: Embora a segurança seja compartilhada, o ônus [[não deve recair apenas no usuário final]]. Nenhum serviço garante segurança completa, mas os danos conhecidos e previstos devem ser [[avaliados no design e na oferta do serviço]].

source.title: Safety by Design Overview (May 2019)
evidence:
This principle is based on the central tenet that

while user safety is a shared responsibility, the

burden of safety should never fall solely upon

the end user. It acknowledges that, even though

no platform or service can ensure the complete

safety of individuals, every attempt should be

made to ensure that known and anticipated harms

have been adequately assessed in the design and

provision of a service.

question: Como o princípio 2 relaciona configurações padrão e autonomia?
answer: O relatório defende funções que permitam ao usuário controlar sua experiência e recomenda [[configurações de privacidade e segurança no nível mais alto por padrão]], já no cadastro. Ressalta que muitos usuários mantêm as configurações iniciais.

source.title: Safety by Design Overview (May 2019)
evidence:
Features and functionality that allow users to

fully govern and regulate their own experiences —

particularly at times when their safety is being, or is

at risk of being, compromised is recommended.

Principle 2.1: Provide technical measures and tools

that allow users to manage their own safety, and

that are set to the most secure privacy and safety

levels by default

In a shared responsibility framework, for users to

have control over their own safety they need to be

provided with the right tools — and feel empowered

to use these tools. In a rights-based framework

such as the SbD Framework, individuals should

be provided with opportunities to revise their

preferences and choices as they see fit. They should

also have control over their personal information

and how it is portrayed.

Our consultation process with young people,

parents and carers highlighted a consumer

expectation that privacy and safety settings should

be placed at the highest levels by default — that

is, at sign-up or registration. This is particularly

important when considering that the vast majority

of users keep privacy settings at the level they were

configured at on registration

question: Que retorno aos usuários o subprincípio 2.4 recomenda no tratamento de denúncias?
answer: [[Funções de suporte e ciclos de feedback]] que informem o estado das denúncias e os resultados das medidas adotadas, com [[oportunidade de recurso]]. A resposta deve também orientar para outras fontes de apoio, reconhecendo o bem-estar e as vulnerabilidades de quem denuncia.

source.title: Safety by Design Overview (May 2019)
evidence:
Principle 2.4: Provide built-in support functions and

feedback loops for users that inform users on the

status of their reports, what outcomes have been

taken and offer an opportunity for appeal

A holistic response to safety concerns is needed:

one that not only deals with the issue or problem at

hand, but also guides the user to additional sources

of support or help. This approach recognises that

user wellbeing can be just as important as user

safety. It also respects the particular vulnerabilities

that might be experienced by users making reports

or complaints, especially when the reporting leaves

them feeling exposed or visible.

question: Qual cautela o relatório estabelece sobre a adoção dos princípios e as notas de boas práticas?
answer: A adoção dos princípios é [[voluntária]]. As notas de boas práticas são [[ilustrações orientadoras]]: o relatório afirma que não há evidência robusta sobre sua efetividade e seu impacto, portanto não devem ser tratadas como intervenções de eficácia comprovada.
